source_title: Remember Patrick Stewart’s Life and Career in Photos - People.com
source_excerpt:
The celebrated actor of ‘Star Trek,’ ‘X-Men’ and stage fame died at age 86 on Oct. 28, 2026
Patrick Stewart entertained the world for more than 60 years.
The actor began his career on stage, becoming a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1969 and making his Broadway debut in 1971. He won his first of two Laurence Olivier Awards in 1979 and a Grammy Award in 1996, and he also picked up nominations for a Tony , three Golden Globes , four Emmy Awards and three SAG Awards over the years.
In television and film, Stewart was best known for his role as Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in the Star Trek franchise from 1987 to 2023, as well as for his portrayal of Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men from 2000 to 2017.
His longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared the news of Stewart’s death on Oct. 29, 2026, announcing that the icon had died at age 86 following a brief journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
Ahead, remember the acclaimed actor’s life and career in photos, from fatherhood and friendship to films and more.
Born in England on July 13, 1940, Sir Patrick Stewart and his two older brothers were raised by his mother, Gladys, a mill worker. His father, Alfred, was a British soldier during World War II who later suffered from PTSD. “We were poor and had almost nothing,” Stewart recalled to PEOPLE in a 2022 interview.
“She was so sweet and caring and loving, a simple soul,” Stewart said of his mother (with him, ca. 1943), who died in 1977. “She’d had no education at all and worked at a big weaving mill for decades.”
Evening Standard/Hulton Archive/Getty
His childhood was a difficult one; he recalled often standing between his father and mother to prevent him from abusing her, “a skill no child should ever have to learn,” he wrote in The Guardian . But at 12, an English teacher suggested he try acting, which became “my own refuge,” he wrote.
Stewart played Launce in the Royal Shakespeare Company’s 1970 production of The Two Gentlemen of Verona, starting a long history of storied theater work, including a 2013 Broadway production of No Man’s Land/Waiting for Godot.
Patrick Stewart on ‘Star Trek: The Next Generation’
Paramount Television/Kobal/Shutterstock
“I think it happened to me at exactly the right time,” Stewart (with the original cast of Star Trek: The Next Generation in 1987) said of finding sudden fame at age 46. His role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard brought him a new level of success; he played the character for the show’s seven popular seasons and in four subsequent feature films. “There is not a corner of my life that wasn’t impacted.”
In 2000, Stewart was tapped to play Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men and went on to star in seven films in the franchise. He will reprise the character in a posthumous appearance in Avengers: Doomsday , set for release on Dec. 18, 2026.
The actor spent a difficult year playing Macbeth opposite Kate Fleetwood at the Brooklyn Academy of Music in 2008.
“Doing the play had a really dark impact on my life. Because he is a tragic figure,” Stewart shared. “Yes, he’s a villain. Yes, he kills people. Yes, he ruins people’s lives, but he is a struggler. I would do the show, and I would get in my car and go home and drink. I really turned into an alcoholic because the only way I could clear my head of this man was by alcohol. I would drink until I passed out. I got help with the drinking. One of the reasons was because I met my wife.”
Patrick Stewart and Wife Sunny Ozell
Stewart and his third wife Sunny Ozell (pictured in Jamaica in 2015) met when she served him in a Brooklyn diner. “It was the only time in my life I’ve given someone my telephone number and said call me,” he told PEOPLE. “I’ve never met anyone like her before. She is so smart and so informed. And her intellectual accomplishments are extraordinary. She remembers everything. My life is perpetually interesting — and it’s largely as a result of Sunny.”
Longtime friend Sir Ian McKellen officiated the couple’s 2013 wedding. The actors starred in the X-Men franchise together, with McKellen playing the occasional villain Magneto.
Stewart has two children with ex-wife Sheila Falconer, Daniel (pictured) and Sophie . “I loved Daniel when he was little, and when he was a baby, I loved holding him. It was fantastic,” Stewart recalled fondly of his son’s early days.
Stewart credits his children for both encouraging him and teasing him on his initial Star Trek audition.
“They thought it was hysterical that I was even auditioning,” he said. “They told me, ‘Dad, we used to watch [the original] every night!’ I said, ‘The guys wearing the colored T-shirts?’ That was all I knew about it.”
After landing the role, “they teased me of course,” said Stewart. “But I think they were actually quite proud that dad was Captain Jean-Luc Picard.”
“When my daughter was born, it just happened to be in a time when my work was slowing down,” Stewart (with Sophie in 2009) remembered to PEOPLE. “The first two years of her life I was very much a caretaker because her mother was a wonderful dancer and appeared in musicals. I took over the job of being mom and dad, and I loved it. It was marvelous.”
When Stewart was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace in 2010, he called the moment an “unlooked-for honor.”
He also paid tribute to the teacher who encouraged him to act, according to the BBC . “Although many people in my life have had great influence on me, without this man none of it would have happened,” he said.
Patrick Stewart on ‘Star Trek: Picard’
Stewart returned to his iconic ‘80s role in 2020 for the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard (the show wrapped this spring after three seasons). “Thirty-three years later and I’m still doing it,” he said. “I’ve been very, very lucky.”
“I thought I’d be retired [by now],” Stewart told PEOPLE in 2022. “It just hasn’t happened.” At some point, though, he and Ozell planned to “go somewhere and just sort of shut down,” he added. “I’m looking forward to it very much. Although, my wife believes I’ll tolerate it for about two weeks. Then I’ll be calling my agent.”
In 2023, the actor opened up about his life story in his memoir Making It So , going in depth about his early life in England and his views on Hollywood at the time of publication.
“There were passages in the book that were painful to write about, but I knew that by writing about them I was doing myself some benefit and that it would be good for me,” Stewart told PEOPLE.
The Olivier Award winner added, “This is the frankest I have been about my life, my passions, my relationships. I do have a tiny wish that the book would give some insights and some encouragement to others.”
On Oct. 28, 2026, Stewart died at his home in Los Angeles “in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” his longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak shared in a statement to PEOPLE. The star was 86.
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” Bush Novak continued. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”

प्रसिद्ध प्रवक्ता केली बुश नोवाक द्वारा People.com के साथ साझा किए गए एक बयान के अनुसार, मंच और परदे के जाने-माने अभिनेता सर पैट्रिक स्टुअर्ट का 28 अक्टूबर, 2026 को 86 वर्ष की आयु में निधन हो गया। घोषणा में बताया गया कि अल्जाइमर रोग और लेवी बॉडी डिमेंशिया से जूझने के बाद लॉस एंजिल्स स्थित उनके घर पर उनका निधन हुआ।

स्थापित मनोरंजन रिपोर्टिंग और उनके संस्मरण के अनुसार, स्टुअर्ट ने इंग्लैंड में अपने शुरुआती जीवन से लेकर थिएटर, टेलीविजन और फिल्मों में दशकों तक प्रशंसित कार्य किया।

## करियर की मुख्य बातें और प्रसिद्ध भूमिकाएँ

* **रंगमंच की शुरुआत:** स्टुअर्ट 1969 में रॉयल शेक्सपियर कंपनी से जुड़े, 1971 में अपना ब्रॉडवे डेब्यू किया, और 1979 में अपना पहला लॉरेंस ओलिवियर पुरस्कार जीता।
* **स्टार ट्रेक:** उन्होंने 1987 में शुरू हुए 'स्टार ट्रेक: द नेक्स्ट जेनरेशन' के सात सीज़न, चार फीचर फिल्मों और बाद की पैरामाउंट+ सीरीज़ 'स्टार ट्रेक:पिकार्ड' में कैप्टन जीन-लुक पिकार्ड की भूमिका निभाई।
* **एक्स-मेन:** उन्होंने एक्स-मेन फ्रेंचाइजी की सात फिल्मों में प्रोफेसर चार्ल्स जेवियर की भूमिका निभाई और 18 दिसंबर, 2026 को रिलीज होने वाली फिल्म 'अवेंजर्स: डूम्सडे' में उनकी एक मरणोपरांत उपस्थिति तय है।

## व्यक्तिगत जीवन और सम्मान

13 जुलाई, 1940 को इंग्लैंड में जन्मे स्टुअर्ट ने साक्षात्कारों और अपने 2023 के संस्मरण 'मेकिंग इट सो' में अपने कठिन बचपन को पार करने के बारे में खुलकर बात की थी। 12 वर्ष की आयु में एक अंग्रेजी शिक्षक ने उन्हें अभिनय आजमाने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया था।

अपने करियर के दौरान, स्टुअर्ट ने एक ग्रैमी पुरस्कार जीता, साथ ही टोनी, तीन गोल्डन ग्लोब, चार एमी और तीन एसएजी पुरस्कारों के लिए नामांकन प्राप्त किए। उन्हें 2010 में बकिंघम पैलेस में महारानी एलिजाबेथ द्वितीय द्वारा नाइट की उपाधि से सम्मानित किया गया था। उनके परिवार में उनकी तीसरी पत्नी सनी ओज़ेल हैं, जिनसे उन्होंने 2013 में विवाह किया था, तथा उनके पूर्व विवाह से दो बच्चे डैनियल और सोफी हैं।

घोषणा के विवरण को सत्यापित करने के इच्छुक पाठक People.com जैसे स्थापित मनोरंजन प्रकाशनों द्वारा रिपोर्ट किए गए आधिकारिक बयानों को देख सकते हैं।

en_body:
According to a statement shared by his longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak with People.com, celebrated stage and screen actor Sir Patrick Stewart died at the age of 86 on Oct. 28, 2026. The announcement stated that he passed away at his home in Los Angeles following a brief journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

Established entertainment reporting and memoir accounts trace Stewart’s life from his upbringing in England to decades of acclaimed work across theater, television, and film.

## Career Milestones and Iconic Roles

* **Stage Roots:** Stewart joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1969, made his Broadway debut in 1971, and won his first Laurence Olivier Award in 1979.
* **Star Trek:** He portrayed Captain Jean-Luc Picard across seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation starting in 1987, four feature films, and the subsequent Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard.
* **X-Men:** He played Professor Charles Xavier in seven films within the X-Men franchise and is slated for a posthumous appearance in Avengers: Doomsday, set for release on Dec. 18, 2026.

## Personal Life and Accolades

Born in England on July 13, 1940, Stewart spoke openly in interviews and his 2023 memoir, Making It So, about overcoming a difficult childhood. An English teacher encouraged him to try acting at age 12, providing what he described as a refuge.

Over his career, Stewart earned a Grammy Award, alongside nominations for a Tony, three Golden Globes, four Emmys, and three SAG Awards. He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace in 2010. He is survived by his third wife, Sunny Ozell, whom he married in 2013 in a ceremony officiated by longtime friend Sir Ian McKellen, as well as his children from a previous marriage, Daniel and Sophie.

Readers wishing to verify details of the announcement can consult official statements reported by established entertainment publications such as People.com.
